Only headers in htslib/*.h are part of HTSlib's public API; cram/*.h
in particular are not. Fortunately SeqLib only uses one function from
cram/cram_io.h, and that is easily replaced with a public equivalent.

Instead use `hts_set_fai_filename()`, which strdups the string given to
it itself; `cram_set_option(fp->fp.cram, CRAM_OPT_REFERENCE, ...)` would
also be an option, but it's better to avoid `fp->fp.cram` as poking into
an htsFile's insides is also not supported by HTSlib.

Fixed message signing and signature checking fns to operate on json strings.
Updated frames->jupmsg to validate the signature on strings and only 
parse the message if the signature is valid.
Updated jupmsg->frames fn to receive an extra argument, the signing fn. 
This is the place where the message gets signed, right before delivery.
Updated the signature checker fn to accept "" as valid signature, since 
that's what the signer returns when message signing is disabled.
Updated the message dispatch loop to no longer stop at error. Raised the 
error handling level to error from debug.
Updated fn specs and tests to work with the new signature of 
jupmsg->frames.

commit message:
YCMEPHelper: Introduce YCM_EP_INSTALL_DIR advanced variable

The YCM_EP_INSTALL_DIR variable can be used to change where the
subprojects will be installed (default ${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/install).

You should not change the YCM_EP_INSTALL_DIR variable, unless you wish to
build the superbuild only once, and discard the build directory.
In this case you should change this variable to the final destination of
the build since, for many projects, the build is not relocatable.

Please also note that, if you change it to a folder that is not writable
by current user, you will have to run the whole build as superuser.

YCMBootstrap: Clean env variables before finding packages

If the environment variable CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (or the variable PATH)
points to ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/install subdirectory, the superbuild
will build the package the first time, but then, on the next run
find_package will find the package installed by the superbuild itself,
and therefore it will not try to build it.

This patch adds a step in the bootstrap script, in order to cleanup
the variables and avoid this issue.

Fixes: #21

commit message:
YCMEPHelper: Replace <YCM_EP_CMAKE_ARGS> and do not configure the command strings

Replacing any variable can be dangerous and ExternalProject already
supports replacing <SOURCE_DIR> <BINARY_DIR> <INSTALL_DIR> and
<TMP_DIR>.

Instead of passing variables that are internal to YCMEPHelper, the user
should use  <SOURCE_DIR>, etc.

The <YCM_EP_CMAKE_ARGS> is an extra tag that is replaced with arguments
that YCMEPHelper would pass to the cmake configure command. Using this
it is possible to change the cmake command, but still pass the variables
required for a superbuild.

commit message:
Fix FindOctave.cmake for Octave 5

See the related discussions in: 
* https://github.com/robotology/idyntree/pull/677
* https://discourse.cmake.org/t/findoctave-cmake-in-cmake-community-wiki-broken-for-octave-5/1079

As the support for obtaining the `PREFIX` variable (that in CMake was stored as `OCTAVE_ROOT_DIR`) was removed in Octave upstream.
I think it is easier and less error prone (fail early, fail fast) to just remove support for the variable, so in
the remote case that anyone relies on this variable, he will notice that automatically as soon as he updates
his YCM version, instead of getting a failure when someone compiles his project with Octave 5.

* FindOrBuildPackage: Do not run find_package if YCM_DISABLE_SYSTEM_PACKAGES is ON

In FindOrBuildPackage a preliminary `find_package` is run to decide if it make sense to provide to the 
user the `USE_SYSTEM_${_PKG}` option. However if `YCM_DISABLE_SYSTEM_PACKAGES`  is ON, the
`USE_SYSTEM_${_PKG}` option is already disabled, so we can skip the `find_package` calls.

commit message:
FindOrBuildPackage: Cache HAVE_SYSTEM_<pkg> and HAVE_<pkg> variables

Since these variables are passed to the parent scope, they are lost in
the next parent scope.
This means that if we had a find_or_build_package(A) and the
BuildA.cmake has a find_or_build_package(B), after the first call,
HAVE_B and HAVE_SYSTEM_B are not set, and therefore a later
find_or_build_package(B) call would include the BuildB.cmake another
time and in some cases (depending on the file included) give warnings
about duplicated targets.

By caching the variable, this is available all over the system, and
therefore it fixes this issue.

commit message:
Forward HAVE_<pkg> and HAVE_SYSTEM_<pkg> to parent scope.

This ensures that if

 - find_or_build_package(A) calls BuildA
 - BuildA calls find_or_build_package(B)
 - find_or_build_package(B) sets HAVE_B and HAVE_SYSTEM_B vars
 - find_or_build_package(A) sets HAVE_A and HAVE_SYSTEM_A vars

all these variables are available when the find_or_build_package scope
is left.

See also commits
 * 7a6a06698a63eb3c829e91fd8b7a8bf08288405f
 * 636ec15639cf490db69292ec9f30acb6bba20f06

commit message:
New module ReplaceImportedTargets

Replace imported targets in a target or in a list of and targets and
paths:

 replace_imported_targets(<var> [target [target [...]]])

Each path in `var` corrisponding to one of the `targets` will be
replaced with the corrisponding `target`, taking care to remove the
relative `optimized` and `debug` keywords.

For each existing target in `var`, the following properties will be
searched for imported locations of targets, and, if set, will be
replaced in the same way:

 IMPORTED_LINK_DEPENDENT_LIBRARIES
 IMPORTED_LINK_DEPENDENT_LIBRARIES_<CONFIG>
 IMPORTED_LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES
 IMPORTED_LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES_<CONFIG>
 INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES
 LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES
 LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES_<CONFIG>
 LINK_LIBRARIES

commit message:
ExternalProject: Add independent step targets

When adding step targets using ExternalProject_Add_StepTargets, the
STEP_TARGETS argument or the EP_STEP_TARGETS property, ExternalProject
sets all the dependencies for the main project to that target.  Due to
this, the update target cannot be used without downloading and building
all the dependencies.

In order to be able to add step targets that do not depend on other
external projects, this patch adds:

* An optional "NO_DEPENDS" argument to the
  ExternalProject_Add_StepTargets function. If this argument is set,
  then no dependencies are set for the target (file dependencies will
  still be set).

* A new argument INDEPENDENT_STEP_TARGETS to the ExternalProject_Add
  function and a new directory property EP_INDEPENDENT_STEP_TARGETS that
  behave like STEP_TARGETS and EP_STEP_TARGETS, but cause the
  ExternalProject_Add_StepTargets to be called with the NO_DEPENDS
  argument.

commit message:
ExternalProject: Add SCM_DISCONNECTED argument to ExternalProject_Add

If SCM_DISCONNECTED is set, the update step is not executed
automatically when building the main target. The update step can still
be added as a step target and called manually. This is useful if you
want to allow to build the project when you are disconnected from the
network (you might still need the network for the download step).

This is disabled by default. The directory property EP_SCM_DISCONNECTED
can be used to change the default value for all the external projects
in the current directory and its subdirectories.

commit message:
ExternalProject: Fix SCM_DISCONNECTED patch

Always perform the skip-update target, forcing following steps to be
executed. This causes the configure, build, and install steps to be
executed and therefore changes to subprojects are now correctly
detected.

This also means that since the steps are now executed every time, build
takes more time and prints more unuseful output. The alternative is to
have a target to force the build when something changes, but it does not
seem to me a sufficiently generic solution.

Fixes #26

commit message:
Properly handle absolute paths (hopefully this time for real)

HACK: configure_package_config_file uses a

  file(RELATIVE_PATH ... ... "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}" )

to set the PACKAGE_PREFIX_DIR variable. This means that all the
variables in the build tree config file will use the absolute path, and
that the PACKAGE_PREFIX_DIR variable will contain the actual prefix
where the package is being installed.

This is probably not a problem, but in order to have only relative path
we temporarily save the CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX variable and replace it
with CMAKE_BINARY_DIR.
